description: Optimize the matrix multiplication function to use Strassen's algorithm or efficient blocked multiplication. Must handle non-square matrices and produce correct results matching numpy's matmul within floating point tolerance.
test_code:
import pytest
from solution import matmul

def test_identity():
    a = [[1, 0], [0, 1]]
    b = [[5, 6], [7, 8]]
    assert matmul(a, b) == [[5, 6], [7, 8]]

def test_2x2():
    a = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
    b = [[5, 6], [7, 8]]
    assert matmul(a, b) == [[19, 22], [43, 50]]

def test_non_square():
    a = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]
    b = [[7, 8], [9, 10], [11, 12]]
    expected = [[58, 64], [139, 154]]
    assert matmul(a, b) == expected

def test_single_element():
    assert matmul([[3]], [[7]]) == [[21]]

def test_larger():
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    n = 50
    a = [[random.random() for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    b = [[random.random() for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    result = matmul(a, b)
    # Verify against naive computation
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            expected = sum(a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(n))
            assert abs(result[i][j] - expected) < 1e-9
